blocks.x: The End The End Babe Phillips, March 25th, 1957, Real 1 This is Joe Phillips. That's loud enough?
Yes, that's good. When were you born?
How old are you? Well, I'm 65.
You can just sit back. Tell them your age. You can just sit back. Just take it easy. Lean back. I ain't eight. Now you know you ain't 65. What year were you born in?
That's one thing. I don't know much.
He is 78 years old right now. 78 years old.
You got a good age. Were you born here in the city? I was born in St. John's Parish. When did you leave St. John's Parish?
I was born in St. John's Parish 19...19...19...19...1918

1918. You left St. John's Parish. See? Now... What was the first kind of music you heard that you remember? Any type of music? When I first come to the city? No, when you first started out when you were a little boy. In the country.
In the country. Well, when I was in the country, I was playing guitar in a band. Oh, yeah. A band by the name of the Magnolia Band. I was playing guitar. The Magnolia? The Magnolia Band.
And...
Who was the leader of the band? Well, it was a first cousin of mine. There was a young man by the name of Casimir Matthew. He was the leader.
Casimir Matthew?
He was the leader of the band. The Magnolia Band.
Did he have a manager too?
Huh? Was he the manager too? He was the manager. He was the manager of the... He was the violin player. He was the manager. I see.
And what towns did you play in?

Oh, I played with the Lord in so many towns. All in the country. I played St. James. I played St. John. I played St. Charles Parish. Played music all different places. We were at Dansonville when I was out there.
Up in Playman Williams territory?
That's right. Playman Williams place. Okay.
I talked to Freddie Landry up there about a year ago. The trombone player. You remember him? He played trombone and piano.
I remember him.
I think his brother's name was Al Seed. You remember the big boy? Yeah. He came down here and worked with the Eureka Band. You remember all those fellas from up there?
That's right.
Who else was in this Magnolia band? How big a band?
Seven Piece Band.
It was the Seedenteenth Band?
Seedenteenth Band. Mm-hmm.
And who else was in it? If I would, what instrumentation did they have? You know, different instruments?
Well, they had a fella they called Fernand Alexander, that was the trumpet player. And now they both the trombone player and then No-No, La Grande. No-No La Grande.
That's right.
The drummer, Romeo and Thomas. Mm-hmm. That was the drummer. Did that? Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
